headline: Ridgefield seller inspection prep.
subhead: A five-step inspection playbook for listing this November. Swipe.

slides.title: Service the heating plant.
slides.text: Have a licensed technician tune the boiler or furnace and stamp the service tag. Buyers test heat on day one.

slides.title: Pump and locate septic.
slides.text: Locate tank lids and pump the tank now before the ground freezes. Keep the cleanout receipt for buyer review.

slides.title: Pull town hall permits.
slides.text: Check Ridgefield Town Hall records for open building, electrical, or plumbing permits on past renovations. Close them out early.

slides.title: Test well water quality.
slides.text: Run a standard potability test through a state-certified lab. Having recent clean lab results avoids delayed mortgage underwriting.

slides.title: Inspect roof and gutters.
slides.text: Clear late fall leaves from gutters and verify flashing around chimneys. Cold rain exposes roof leaks quickly during buyer walkthroughs.

caption:
Most home sale delays in Ridgefield come down to surprise septic or permit issues during buyer inspections.

If you plan to sell your house in Ridgefield CT this winter, run through the basic mechanicals before listing.

Ground frost makes septic inspections harder once December arrives. Town hall permit records take time to clear if an old project was never signed off. Getting your furnace serviced and water tested this month takes the leverage away from buyers during contract negotiations.
